note: Each aircraft type's lamps (to-do 243, 2026-11-24), read by one function for every aircraft (AircraftLights.cpp: AI traffic, parked, later the player's own). In the model's own cm like aircraft-doors.json: x its right, y aft (the nose is -y), z up, the root at the nose wheel on the ground. A320 lamp places (2026-11-28): FlightGear A320-common.xml light offsets and compositor beam directions, mapped as Art/A320/make_a320_fg.py places the model (quarter turn, nose wheel to the origin, 0.24 deg pitch, 0.30 m strut compression); logo lamps on the tailplane top 2 m out aimed at the fin, wing lamps aimed at the slat edge 9 m out (FlightGear has neither aim). "on": "nose-gear" = on the nose strut: folds with it, lit only when down and locked. group: beacon, strobe, nav, logo, landing, takeoff, taxi, turnoff, wing-scan, engine-scan, cabin-window - when each group is on comes from the switching (SimTraffic Blink, parked: ADPAircraftLights::Parked). at: the lamp; dir: where it shines (omitted = all round); cone: half angle of the beam (deg); color: linear rgb; glow: the lamp face's brightness, size its size (m); skin: how strongly it lights the aircraft's own skin and what is round it (a light decal, no light source - every aircraft, any distance), reach: how far that goes (m); pool: true = the beam's pool on the ground ahead (landing, taxi, turn-off), the soft decal far away, a real spot light (lumens, range m) on the nearest aircraft, faded between unseen. A320: nav/beacon/strobe/landing/taxi/turn-off places measured on Art/A320/A320.glb (2026-11-21); tail strobe, logo, wing and engine scan estimated from the A320's published dimensions (not measured on the model). No cabin-window lamps until to-do 209's cabin is in the game.
